evidence: Cic. Off. 1.39: fidem hostī datam fallere
Cic. Off. 1.23: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs
terms.comment: Fidem dare, to give one’s word (Cic. Rab. Perd. 28); fidem servāre, to keep it (Caes. BG 6.36); fidem fallere or frangere, to break it (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 3.92: pacta et prōmissa servāre (Lewis & Short s.v. prōmittō)
Traupman p. 106: to keep promises; to break promises, prōmissa servāre; prōmissa frangere
terms.comment: Prōmissa servāre, to keep one’s promises (Cic., in Morgan–Owens).

evidence: Ter. And. 211: Cui verba dare difficile est.
terms.comment: A false friend: verba dare alicui is to fob someone off with words, to cheat him (Lewis & Short), not to give one’s word.

phrases.latin: ad supplicium redīre māluit quam fidem hostī datam fallere
phrases.english: he chose to go back to be put to death rather than break the word he had given the enemy

phrases.latin: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs, id est dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās
phrases.english: and the foundation of justice is good faith: that is, standing by what has been said and agreed, and being true to it
